items.title: Exercise 1.7: actual perturbation law and finite KL (supporting step)

source.anchor: Exercise 1.7 / (1.E.1), printed p.43 / PDF p.55; reused by Corollary 2.1.2, printed p.50 / PDF p.62
source.attribution: Sinho Chewi's exercise; original ASTIS elaboration of a supporting construction, not a copied source passage or complete exercise answer.

items.statement: The linearization route uses the actual measure with density 1+epsilon*f relative to the reference probability law. For a bounded centered measurable real test, sufficiently small real epsilon makes this density at least one half almost everywhere, defines a probability law, and gives finite canonical KL equal to the compensated entropy integral. This item isolates that supporting construction; the source KL asymptotic and final Poincare conclusion are not asserted by it.
assumptions: The reference law is a probability measure, and the real test is bounded and centered. Smooth compact tests in the literal hint are special cases.
Corollary2.1.2 uses bounded smooth centered tests with compact gradient support, not necessarily compact support of the function.

This generic supporting theorem needs only a.e. strong measurability and an a.e. finite uniform bound. It proves positivity, mass one, RN identification, entropy integrability and canonical KL finiteness rather than assuming them.

obligations.label: Small-parameter positivity, actual unit-mass law, RN representative and finite canonical KL formula
Compose with the separate actual compensated integral limit
Actual Fisher limit, LSI admissibility and final PI/core domain

bindings.boundary: Only the actual perturbation law and finite canonical KL identity. No full KL limit, Fisher, LSI/PI, whole exercise or Bench QA admission.

assumption_deltas.source: A bounded centered smooth compact test in the hint, and bounded centered compact-gradient tests in the second consumer.
assumption_deltas.lean: Any measurable carrier and a.e.-strongly-measurable real f with a finite a.e. uniform bound and zero mean under a probability law.
assumption_deltas.reason: This measure-theoretic construction does not need smoothness, Euclidean geometry or compact support. Their analytical producers and later domain obligations remain separate.

assumption_deltas.source: Sufficiently small positive perturbations give the source probability law.
assumption_deltas.lean: An ordinary two-sided neighborhood of zero, including zero, with a.e. density at least one half and literal withDensity(ofReal) semantics.
assumption_deltas.reason: The bound is produced without dividing by M or epsilon; the actual KL equality is in ENNReal and proves finiteness rather than relying on totalized toReal.
